  shatter, `sub_080C5FA0`/`sub_080C610C` peeked creature and
  `sub_080C61F4` lid as `src/runtime/aos/enemies/ukoback.c`.
  The pot hops on a `umod(random, 0x168) + 0x50` cooldown,
  peeks up to eight creatures (song 0x78 in the centred box),
  and shatters on the lethal blow (song 0x72, direct frame 9,
  sink at `vy 0x8000`, lid child on the `sub_0806D518` blink).
  Resources tiles `0x081F425C`, palette `0x0820BEA4`, frames
  `0x0824D198`, exported as `ukoback` in `objects.c`; two new
  child roles (`UKOBACK_CREATURE`, `UKOBACK_LID`).

  shard entities are `AOS_EFFECT_BURST_15` drifts (same
  special-15 row-7 art), the room-edge bounce uses screen
  margins for the native scroll/probe checks, the creature's
  `+0x14` drift is a fixed countdown, and the lid's sunk mark
  uses the fall timer.
- Verified in game in `area_07_room_010`: three hits on Soma
  (76 + 88 + 88 damage).

  comparison.

## Patch 0961 - Alura Une ported (id 77)

- `EnemyAluraUneCreate` (0x0807C0A0) /
  `EnemyAluraUneUpdate` (0x0807CF9C) plus the scythe-phase handler
  (sub_0807C150), blade-phase handler (sub_0807C494), materialize
  (sub_0807C888), hurt (sub_0807C8FC), scythe spawn/update
  (sub_0807C9A4 / sub_0807CAD4) and orbit-blade spawn/update
  (sub_0807CC9C / sub_0807CDA8) are ported as
  `src/runtime/aos/enemies/alura_une.c` with two new child roles
  (scythe, orbit blade) wired through `aria_runtime.c`.
- Both fight phases run the native 14-entry sub-state machine on
  + 0x0B: state 0 throws scythe volleys, state 1 throws the delayed
  fan and emits orbit blades on the + 0x6E frame words 3 and 4;
  state 2 is the shared generic death, state 3 the materialize.
- Resources from the ROM: tiles 0x081CBF9C, palette 0x0820A674,
  frames 0x08218D3C. Songs 0x6A (first hurt), 0x6E (death) and 0x80
  (orbit blade) are requested at the native points; unit-tested in
  `alura_une_tests`.
- Verified in game in `area_10_room_003`: the boss aggros, throws
  scythes and orbit blades — four hits for 75-84 damage observed and
  Soma killed at frame 411; captures at frames 300/500 show the
  animated fight.

  ported through SkillAluraUneUse. Divergences are listed in

## Patch 0884 - The editor's transitions in the Aria runtime

- `fusion_aria_runtime` now plays the room document's transitions to Aria
  rooms. A door adopted from a native screen-edge transition redirects
  that entry to the transition's room; any other project door takes Soma
  when his body touches its rectangle, and waits for him to step out
  before firing again. Soma arrives with his feet at the spawn point or,
  without one, beside the saved target door. Transitions to Zero Mission
  are skipped; a door off the 8-pixel grid, an entry the room lacks or a
  transition with no arrival has the document's doors ignored.
- Checked on captures in area 0 room 1: a new door leads to room 2 at its
  spawn point; the right-edge entry redirected to room 5 arrives at its
  spawn point, and leads to room 2 again without overlays. ROM-free tests
  cover the mapping, the target-door arrival and the rejections.
- Limitations: door types have no effect, and Aria's tiles stay native.

## Patch 0883 - The editor's entities in the Aria runtime

- `fusion_aria_runtime` now adds the room document's entities that have an
  Aria native reference (`enemy:HH`, `special-object:HH`,
  `generic-candle:HH`, `pickup:HH` and the hard-mode and all-souls pickup
  families) to the room's entities, at the centre of their 16-pixel box. A
  pickup takes its item from `item_id` and its collection flag from
  `parameter_0`; the runtime plays the kinds it has ported. A document with
  an entity outside the room or an unknown reference is ignored.
- Checked on a capture in area 0 room 1: a placed bat and a Potion appear,
  and Soma collects the Potion. ROM-free tests cover the reference mapping,
  the position, the item fields and the rejections.
- Limitations: the runtime keeps collection flags 0 to 191 only, so a
  pickup above them never appears; Aria's tiles and doors stay native.

## Patch 0882 - The editor's collision in the Aria runtime

- New `aos_room_overlay`: `fusion_aria_runtime` now plays the collision
  painted in the editor. The room's project document
  (`overrides/aria/entities/area_<AA>_room_<NNN>.json`, 8-pixel cells) has
  its cells replace the native BG1 collision bytes with their type's byte
  (solid 0x03, one-way 0x01, rising slope 0x45, falling slope 0x41, air
  0x00). A document of another room or size, or with water or hazard
  cells, which the runtime cannot play yet, is reported and ignored.
  `--no-overlays` and `--overlay-dir DIR` work as in Zero Mission.
- New `project_room_document`: the project document loader shared by both
  runtimes.
- Checked on captures in area 0 room 1: Soma stops at a painted wall and
  falls through a painted hole; the native room is unchanged without
  overlays. ROM-free tests cover the byte mapping and every rejection.
- Limitations: Aria's pre-composited backgrounds do not show the painted
  collision, and its tiles, entities and doors stay native.

## Patch 0881 - The editor's transitions in the Zero Mission runtime

- The room's project document now also plays its transitions to Zero
  Mission rooms: a door adopted from a native door (`native_source`) is
  redirected to the transition's room, and any other project door becomes a
  new hatchless transition over its blocks (a side door for left and right,
  a vertical transition for up and down). Samus arrives with her feet at the
  spawn point or, without one, beside the saved target door. Transitions to
  Aria are skipped; a door off the block grid or a transition with no
  arrival has the document's doors ignored.
- Checked on captures: a new door in Brinstar's save room leads to room 31
  at its spawn point; native door 71 redirected to room 29 arrives beside
  the target project door, and leads to room 31 again without overlays.
  ROM-free tests cover the mapping, the target-door arrival and the
  rejections.
- Limitations: door types (boss, locked, portal, save) have no effect, an
  adopted door keeps its native geometry and hatch, and events stay native.

  not ported. The companion is emitted by the first update.
  No emulator comparison.
- Unit-tested in waiter_skeleton_tests: create and flag
  state, the companion attach and hide, the wake, both tray
  branches' shared path, the throw with song 0x89 and the
  armed contact, the burst, the walk to idle and the
  7-piece death.

## Patch 0877 - Waiter Skeleton decoded (id 30, not yet ported)

Decode-only checkpoint; nothing is implemented yet. The family is the
largest single-enemy chain ported so far (~1400 asm lines): the parent
plus two linked children of entity type 0x1B / role 0x48 allocated by
sub_0806DFF8 (0x1B/0x48 normally, 0xD0/0xDF under the global 0x8E &
0x40 inert flag).

- EnemyWaiterSkeletonCreate (0x080AF574): tiles 0x081E4194,
  palette 0x0820BE3C, frames 0x082393E0; sets + 0x20 bit 1, spawns the
  companion child sub_080AEC0C, copies + 0x3C / + 0x34, plays
  animation 0, + 0x5C = 0x13, element-1 contact sub_0806E1B8, hurt
  sub_080AF6FC, floor snap sub_0806AF98, + 0x46 += 1, + 0x59 bit 1;
  global inert -> state 4, else state 0.
- EnemyWaiterSkeletonUpdate (0x080AF650): pause gate sub_0806CC20,
  states 0-4 then the shared sub_0806E314 / sub_0806DF20 tail.
  - State 0: sub_0806BC40 facing; while + 0xB == 0 the centred wake
    box sub_0806CFFC(+ 0x42 - 0xA0, + 0x46 - 0x28, 0x140, 0x50)
    enters state 1 (+ 0xC = + 0xB = 0).
  - State 1 sub_080AF194, step machine + 0xB cases 0-4: case 0 picks
    branch on RNG & 3 (== 0 -> case 1, else case 3); cases 1 and 3
    each spawn a tray child sub_080AED28 via sub_0806DFF8 with
    + 0x14 = 0x11 (case 1, then anim 6, step 2) or + 0x14 = 9
    (+ 0x20 bit 0 set, anim 7, step 4); cases 2 and 4 share the tail
    that waits for the animation-end flag + 0x6C & 4, replays
    animation 3 looping and returns to state 2.
  - State 2 sub_080AF2A0, step machine + 0xB cases 0-5 on the
    sub_0806CAF8 walker with probe table 0x08528608: case 0 walks at
    speed 0x8000 and the near box (+ 0x42 - 0x64, + 0x46 - 0x28,
    0x190, 0x50) triggers anim 4 with RNG & 3 choosing step 1 (3/4)
    or a 0x14-tick repeat; case 1 walks faster, the tighter box
    (+ 0x42 - 0x50, 0x140 wide) plays anim 5 and goes to step 2;
    case 2 sets + 0x20 bit 2 while + 0x6E == 2 (contact window),
    clears + 0x20 bits 1-2 on animation end, goes to step 5, replays
    anim 1 and arms + 0xD = 0x3C + (RNG & 0xF); cases 3-5 walk
    backwards at -speed counting + 0xD down (case 3 re-arms 0x32 and
    anim 3 at zero, case 4 falls to step 0, case 5 returns to state 0
    with anim 0). Cases 3-4 appear unreachable from case 2's step-5
    transition; ported as decoded.
  - State 3 sub_080AF450 death: step 0 plays song 0x6B and flings
    0xA debris pieces (0xB when + 0x20 bit 1 is clear) of type
    0x49 / role 0xCF through sub_0806C5AC at the parent position
    (vx = (RNG & 0xF - 8) << 0xE, vy = (RNG & 0xF - 8) << 0xC -
    0x28000, + 0x54 = 0x2000, same tiles/palette merge, + 0xD =
    0x28 + RNG & 0xF), sets the parent fade byte + 0x58 bit 0x20 and
    step 1; step 1 returns 1 so the dispatcher deletes the parent.
  - State 4 only steps the animation (sub_0803F17C).
- Hurt sub_080AF6FC: only when sub_0806E218 applies a blow - it
  computes the damage itself (sub_08021530 / sub_0806B7D8), sets
  the + 0x2D hit timer, subtracts + 0x34 HP and returns lethal; on
  lethal the callback runs sub_080683BC, merges palette bits into
  + 0x5A ((+ 0x2C & 0xF) << 3 | + 0x5A & ~0x79), arms + 0xD = 0x28,
  enters state 3 with + 0xB = + 0xC = 0.
- Companion child sub_080AEC0C (~140 lines): hides (+ 0x59 bit 3)
  while the parent is in state 3 or + 0x20 bit 1 is clear; state 0
  loads the same tiles/palette/frames, sets + 0x59 bit 1, copies
  + 0x5C and plays anim 0x11; state 1 anchors itself to the parent
  through sub_0806C3F8 (the current frame's attach point, index 0)
  plus the parent's + 0x42 / + 0x46, copies the facing bit and
  replays anim 0 whenever the parent's + 0x20 bit 3 is set and its
  own + 0x6D != 8; higher states only run the palette merge and the
  animation step.
- Tray child sub_080AED28 (~560 lines, the big one): preamble forces
  state 5 when its + 0x34 life runs out and, while state <= 2,
  converts to the flying state 3 (clears facing bits, + 0x5C = 0x13,
  installs contact sub_080AF740 / despawn sub_080AF784 through
  sub_0804277C type 0xA, box preset 0x0808FCFC, + 0x72 bits) when its
  + 0x10 palette id differs from the parent's or the parent reaches
  state 5. Case 0 loads the same resources and, after a sub_0803E654
  draw-side check that can delete it, seeds facing/anim bits, + 0x59
  bits 1+4, the parent + 0x5C, anim index + 0x14 (0x11 or 9), the
  facing-dependent + 0x52 offset (+/- 0xA) and the spawn anchor
  (+ 0x42 = parent + 0x42 + offset, + 0x46 = parent + 0x46 - 0x10);
  parent + 0x20 bit 0 set -> state 2 directly. Case 1 mirrors the
  parent while + 0x10 matches and the parent's + 0x6D is 2-5 through
  the per-frame attach table 0x0811937C (x +/- byte 2, y +/- byte 3,
  facing byte 0) and, when the parent's + 0x20 bit 2 is set, plays
  song 0x89, arms the throw (vx from sub_0806CD38 aim vs the player,
  + 0x48 speed, + 0x4C = 0xFFFE0000, + 0x54 = 0x2000, facing bit)
  entering state 2? - the throw path sets state via + 0xA and falls
  into the shared tail; case 2 detaches on palette/parent-state
  change (+ 0x6E == 1 bumps + 0x5C, == 3 copies it and offsets -0xA)
  or state 5. Case 3 is the flight: + 0x48 = +/- 0x8000 by facing,
  + 0x4C = 0xFFFD8000, + 0x54 = 0x2000, song 0x89, then per frame
  + 0x20 += + 0x48 >> 6, sub_0806D490 / sub_0806D384 / sub_0806D3C0 /
  sub_0806D3CC physics, despawn check sub_0806D128 and, on floor or
  margin exit, sub_0806D5C0 effect + sub_0803E6BC + delete. Case 4
  integrates + 0x20 into the draw spin (sub_0803E058) with the
  sub_080421AC tail; case 5 spawns the sub_0806D5C0 burst at + 0x40 /
  + 0x44 with spin + 0x58 & 0x1F, calls sub_0803E6BC and deletes.
  Contact sub_080AF740 deals the parent's + 0x3C through
  sub_08021654 type field and flags the parent + 0x20 bit 3 when the
  palette ids match; sub_080AF784 clears + 0x34 (the life the
  preamble watches); sub_080AF78C is a second contact installing
  sub_08021654 type 1 and recording the hit entity.
- Shared/native approximations still to resolve at port time:
  sub_0806C3F8 frame attach points (no exported anchor table yet -
  fall back to the frame box centre or add the anchor export),
  box presets 0x0808FCFC / 0x0202E8EE via exported frame boxes,
  sub_0803E058 / sub_0803E654 / sub_0803E6BC / sub_0803B9D0 draw
  calls approximated by the standard renderer, sub_080421AC /
  sub_0806D128 margin and floor probes via the existing helpers,
  the + 0x34 tray life source, and the 0x08528608 probe table.
- Resources to export: waiter_skeleton tiles 0x081E4194, palette
  0x0820BE3C, frames 0x082393E0 (the children reuse the same set);
  sounds 0x89 at the tray throw.
- Estimated port size ~800-900 lines of C plus tests; do it as its
  own cycle. Enemy id 30, stats row: hp 120, contact 22, defence 14,
  weak 0x0020, resist 0x0010, soul type 0 index 19 (red soul).

- Create: animation 0 looping, + 0x5C = 0x13, the global
  0x8E & 0x40 path is state 4; otherwise element-1
  contact (sub_0806E1E8), hurt sub_080BB7E4 (lethal only:
  state 3), + 0x72 bit 1 set and the linked orbit child —

  and the animation step, state 4 animation only.
- State 1 sub_080BB2D4 rocks on the floor with the
  sub_0806CAF8 walker (mode 0): + 0x18 counts the phase,
  + 0x54 = sine(phase << 0xB) / 0x30 and the speed is
  + 0x14 (0x100-0x1FF seeded) times sine(phase * 0x300)
  >> 8, negated by + 0xC; while Soma attacks within
  0x4F px and both facings match, phase = 0x30 and + 0xD
  = 1; past phase 0x2F the 0xA0 x 0x46 box starts the
  attack or the walk turns around (animation 2/7, fresh

  cleared (contact live for the dash) and song 0x89;
  its end emits the sub_080BB054 afterimage, restores
  + 0x72, clears + 0x1A bit 1 and plays animation 5;
  animation 5's end returns to the patrol.
- State 3 sub_080BB664: animation 6, song 0x6D, a
  sub_08045CEC gore drift (kind 0x16, preset 8, unit
  direction at a random angle, ax/ay = v / 0x18, vflip)
  every fourth tick; animation end deletes.
- The orbit child sub_080BB0F0 keeps still frame 0x12
  hidden until the parent's + 0x1A bit 0, then orbits 8
  px to the facing side: + 0x1C scale grows 0x1000/frame
  (tracked, not drawn) while + 0x1A spins 0x300/frame —
  mapped to `angle` for the renderer — shrinking 0x2000
  and spinning 0x200 in the pulse state; the parent's
  state 3 or hit flash ends/freezes it.
- The afterimage sub_080BB054 plays animation 8 once,
  following the parent 12 px to its back and 4 px down,
  deleting at the animation end.
- killer_mantle_tests covers create, the orbit-child
  emission and activation, the patrol-to-attack
  transition, the dash kinematics and song, the ghost
  lifecycle, the orbit spin, the lethal death with gore
  and the flag-path state 4.
- Divergences: the orbit scale is not drawn, the + 0x58
  fade and + 0x59 / + 0x5A / + 0x5C bookkeeping, the box
  presets, the sub_0806E3B0 / sub_0806BBC4 reads

  0x0802B9A9) has no ported update yet.

## Patch 0873 - Dryad decoded (id 70, not yet ported)

- EnemyDryadCreate (0x080AEAAC) /
  EnemyDryadUpdate (0x080AEB8C) in
  third_party/cvaos/asm/code/code_080A0A8C.s, plus the

  Dryad spits a seed (entity type 0x1B, role 0x48) that

  0x082388AC; animation 0 loop; the global 0x8E & 0x40
  path is state 4 (animation only); otherwise floor
  snap, + 0x46 += 1, + 0x59 |= 2, state 0, contact
  sub_080AEB50 (contact element is the entity + 0x3C
  byte through sub_08021654) and hurt sub_080AE3FC.
- State 0 sub_080AE4BC (notice): step 0 mirrors the
  facing from sub_0806CF2C bit 0 into + 0x58 bit 6 and
  runs the player box sub_0806CFFC centred
  (+ 0x42 - 0x6E, + 0x46 - 0x28) sized 0xDC x 0x50;
  step 1 repeats the facing write and on RNG & 3 == 0

  substep cleared.

  animation-end flag (+ 0x6C & 4) then plays animation
  2 loop; step 1 runs the generic mover sub_08068AD4
  (-0x80, -0x1F0, 0x1A0) each tick - on its zero return
  it clears a gEwramData ledger dword (0x3D4 +
  (+ 0x37 >> 5) * 4, mask 1 << (+ 0x37 & 0x1F)) and
  sets + 0x59 |= 8, otherwise it faces the player and
  on RNG & 7 == 0 plays animation 3 once with timer
  + 0xD = 0x12 and step 2; step 2 decrements the timer
  and while the post-decrement value is <= 2 plays

  returns to state 0 with step and substep cleared.
- State 3 sub_080AE650 (death): step 0 sets timer
  + 0xD = 0x40, advances to step 1 and draws the
  sub_0803E654 sign bit into the + 0x58 low-5 fade when
  non-negative and sets + 0x59 |= 0x10; step 1 at
  timer 0x10 sets + 0xF = 1, every eighth tick plays
  song 0x6E and calls sub_0806D5C0 at
  (x, y - 16.0, 0x40000, + 0x5C - 1), the timer counts
  to zero then sets + 0x59 |= 8, + 0x58 |= 0x20 and,
  when + 0x59 & 0x10 was set, runs the sub_0803E6BC
  fade and clears the bit; the shared tail runs the

  facing bit 0x40 into + 0x58, offsets the spawn by

## Patch 0863 - Worm family decode (GiantWorm 62 / PoisonWorm 71)

- EnemyGiantWormCreate (0x080AE360) and EnemyPoisonWormCreate
  (0x080AE378) are stubs sharing sub_080AD7F0(e, variant):
  variant 0 brown, 1 poison. Both updates alias
  sub_080AE0E0, a seven-state machine on e+0xA.
- Update head: state 0 only resets to itself; otherwise
  sub_08021924 tracking, sub_0806AD24 hit stun (8 frozen
  frames while alive, then sub_08021278 + sub_080421AC
  collision without the state machine), state != 3 runs
  sub_0806AE54.
- State 1 (wait): +0x1D counts down; at 0 the centred
  sub_0806CFFC box (+0x42-0xA0, +0x46-0x3C, 0x140 x 0x78)
  decides - inside: RandomNumberGenerator & 1 or, with the
  gEwramData + 0x13168 target set and its +0x40 left of the
  worm, facing +0x1F = 0 else 1; outside: pure RNG & 1.
  +0x1D reload and state 2.
- State 2 (emerge): sub_080ADB94(e, +0x1F, 0, 0) then
  sub_080AD9FC; step +0xB == 0 -> state 1.
- State 3 (move): +0x1C = 1, position += velocity
  (+0x48/+0x4C), +0x4C += 0x2000, +0x54 angle adjusted by
  the +0x58 facing bit (0xFFFFFF00 / +0x100 subpixel
  steps); every +0xD & 7 == 0 a sub_0806D5C0 particle at
  (+0x40, +0x44) with (+0x5C - 2); +0xD counts to 0.
- States 4/5: timers; at 0 the +0x58 low five bits feed
  sub_0803E6BC then EntityDelete (state 6 is the
  graphics-only affine variant: sub_0803E058 with the
  mirrored angle bits, sub_0803F17C, no collision).
- Remaining for the port: sub_080AD7F0 (resources, +0x1C
  record), sub_080ADB94 / sub_080AD9FC (the emerge/dive
  sequences), sub_0806CFFC box semantics, sub_0806D5C0
  particle kind, sub_0803E058 affine mapping and the
  +0x1C-driven attack/hurt boxes of the shared epilogue
  (sub_08042848 / sub_080428B4 / sub_0806E314 pattern seen
  in the Golem too).
- Worm create decoded (sub_080AD7F0(e, variant)): segmented
  enemy - +0x59 |= 2, random facing bits into +0x58 low
  five, +0x59 |= 0x10, sub_080ADB0C, +0x14 = self, then
  FOUR children through sub_0806DFF8(e, sub_080ADC2C):
  each takes random facing bits, +0x20 from the parent,
  +0x59 |= 0x10, +0x22 = index << 12, +0x14 = parent,
  +0x18 = parent + 0x59 block, +0x1E = index, x = parent
  +0x40 +/- 0xA0000 by facing, the enemy id byte +0x36 and
  stats via sub_0806B04C. Parent then loads graphics
  0x081E4184, palette 0x0820B724 bank = variant
  (sub_08068264), frames 0x08237C44 (sub_0803B924),
  animation 3 loop for variant 0 else animation 0,
  sub_0803E058 affine init, +0x21 = variant, +0x5C = 0x11,
  state 6 under the global 0x8E & 0x40, else hit callbacks
  sub_080AE334 / sub_080AD748 and state 0. The parent's
  +0x4 = sub_080AE390 links the children.
- Child update sub_080ADC2C decoded (~4 states): header copies
  the parent's +0x5A palette bits (& 0x78); a live child with
  a live non-dying parent runs the hit-stun gate (parent
  +0x2D or sub_0806D4C0 -> sub_08021278 + sub_080429D0, the
  child collision variant; else sub_08021278(1)). State 0
  initialises lazily (skipped when the parent +0x1C record is
  set -> state 3): graphics 0x081E4184 + frames 0x08237C44
  under the parent's +0x2C palette byte, facing bit copied,
  animation 1 (2 for segment index 4), +0x5C = 0x11, state 4
  under the global flag, hit callbacks sub_080AE334 /
  sub_080AE3CC (variant) + sub_080AD748, boxes 0x1010F8F8 via
  sub_080428F0 / sub_08042884, then state 1. State 1 runs the
  emerge pair sub_080ADB94(e, parent+0x1F, parent step, 1) +
  sub_080AD9FC; facing sets sl = +/-0x8000 and, with the
  parent +0x1C set, state 2 with timer 0x38, +0x54 = sl,
  +0x48 = (index << 15) - 0x6000 and +0x4C = -0x30000, vy
  clamped when passing the +0x13110 target's +0x40. State 2
  integrates position, +0x4C += 0x2000, +0x54 angle by
  facing (+/-0x100 subpixel), sub_0806D5C0 particles every
  +0xD & 7 == 0, timer to 0 -> state 3. State 3 deletes when
  the +0x58 low bits & 0x101F are clear after sub_0803E6BC,
  else the +0x22 sine phase (sub_080009E4 * 3 << 13) feeds
  the affine sub_0803E058 with sl +/-0x8000 - the same
  pattern closes state 4 (inert affine-only).
- Emerge/dive decoded: sub_080ADB94 launches each child
  horizontally (vx +/-0x8000 by +0x1F facing, ax -/+0x300),
  holds until vx crosses 0, waits 0x10 ticks and relaunches;
  sub_080AD9FC settles the child on the floor
  (sub_08001D94 height query at room pos + 0xA, +0x46 +=
  result + 2, wall probes sub_0800207C / sub_08002058 at
  x -/+0x18, y - 8 by facing, parent +0x1D = 4 when buried);
  sub_080ADB0C is the create-time floor snap (<= 3 passes at
  y - 8 + 0xA, skipped under the global 0x8E & 0x40).
- Helper semantics resolved: sub_08068A70(e, target) is
  ArcTan2 over the +0x42/+0x46 box-centre deltas (angle to
  target); sub_0806D5C0(x, y, rx, ry) spawns effect entity
  0x49/0xCF via EntityCreateInRange at x + RNG % rx - rx/2,
  y + RNG % ry - ry/2 with a random facing bit (the shared
  dust/particle helper); sub_08021278 registers the entity
  in the tracked list at 0x13170 indexed by 0x131B4 with a
  flag byte at 0x131AC; sub_0803E058 is the affine/OAM slot
  allocator over the 0x03001458 table (<= 0x1F slots, sine /
  cosine via sub_080009E4); sub_080429D0 copies the child's
  +0x74..+0x76 record bytes into a stack struct — the
  tracked-collision registration for linked segments.
- Hit callbacks resolved: sub_080AE334 (Giant Worm segment)
  and sub_080AE3CC (Poison Worm segment) both build the
  standard damage struct (+0x3C type byte, position +0x40/
  +0x44) and call sub_08021654 — the shared Soma damage
  resolver already ported (Blocking Mail path included).
  sub_080AD748 is the segment->parent damage handler:
  damage via sub_08021530 / sub_0806B7D8, parent +0x2D = 8
  hit-stun, parent HP +0x34 reduced; at HP <= 0 it runs
  sub_080683BC palette flash, PlaySong 0x70, merges the
  parent palette byte (+0x2C & 0xF << 3 | +0x5A & -0x79),
  sets parent state 3, +0xD = 0x40 and vx = -0x8000 —
  hitting any segment wounds the whole worm. The
  sub_080AE390 cleanup walks the +0x20-indexed entity
  chain (stride 0xE4, 5 entries) calling sub_0803AC40.
  EnemyGiantWormCreate/Update and EnemyPoisonWormCreate/
  Update confirmed as thin variant wrappers (0 / 1).
- Parent +0x1C resolved: it is a byte flag, not a record —
  the state-3 handler (_080AE21C, the lunge: position +=
  velocity, +0x4C += 0x2000 gravity) sets it, and every
  linked child reads parent +0x1C to switch from the
  emerge branch to its own attack motion (child state 2).
- Still open for the port: the sub_080429D0 +0x74..+0x76
  record layout (tracked-collision registration) and
  resources for ids 62/71 (enemies.tsv rows exist; the
  ENTITY/PROBES rows are not yet in objects.c). The port
  additionally needs runtime support that may not exist
  yet: linked child entities (Bone-Pillar precedent), the
  affine slot table, and the tracked-entity list.
- Golem family recon: EnemyGolemUpdate sub_0807E35C is a
  four-state dispatcher whose state 0 sub_0807E8EC is a
  42-case sub-state machine (~3 KB asm) - boss-scale, not
  a quick family port.

## Patch 0846 - Secret-room map marks moved to the wall break

- Opening the quick map no longer marks secret-room cells — that was

  by the entity record's byte-9 direction: 2 mirrors Y and steps X,
  1 mirrors Y, 4 steps Y) then sub_08012048 sets the table bit.

  wall update; the mark waits on the entity until the main loop,

- Wall `param0` is `(direction << 8) | entry_index` natively; all
  extracted walls currently use direction 0, but the transform is
  ported for completeness.
- Unit tests cover all four direction cases plus a non-table cell.

## Patch 0843 - Obtain-window reward lists decoded

- The obtain/reward window's data path is now fully mapped: the

  entries point to count-prefixed byte-index lists; each index
  resolves through `0x085269FC`'s 4-byte records (kind byte: 2 = item
  `0x08505B3C` stride 16, 3 = weapon `0x08505D3C` stride 28,
  4 = armor `0x085063B0` stride 20, first u16 = name text index).
- ROM dump of the 24 lists: indices 0-2 are large rewards of 18, 31
  and 38 mixed item/equipment entries (story or boss-rush tier
  rewards); indices 3 and up alternate single `item:4`/`item:1`

## Patch 0842 - Drop-context flags identified as boss-rush state

- `sub_080683BC`'s two remaining gates are both boss-rush flags, set
  only by `GameModeBossRushMenuUpdate` (the hidden post-game mode):
  `unk_60.unk_4CC_0` (bits 0-1 of `gEwramData + 0x4CC`) skips the whole
  reward — no experience, bestiary bit or drop — and
  `unk_60.unk_A1_4` (the high nibble of `+0xA1`) raises the
  unowned-soul drop chance from 6 to 7 and scales the damage
  calculation by 8/10.

  `soul_flag_a1 = false` arguments already match the native values;

## Patch 0838 - The 0x131B8 & 0x400 lock identified: Chaos's soul strip

- sub_08031F3C's remaining gate flag is set by sub_08022184, called

  SetPlayerInput). The routine ORs 0x700 into the player flag word —

## Patch 0837 - Character-name easter eggs decoded (JULIUS / NOSOUL / NOUSE)

- The file-load name check (sub_080083C8, mirrored in code_08005894)
  compares the save's 8-byte character name at gEwramData + 0x94
  against three font-encoded names (charset 0x02-0x22 = A-Z):
  - "JULIUS" (0x080E0DCC) sets currentCharacter = 1 — the Julius
    mode unlock, not ported per project constraints.
  - "NOSOUL" (0x080E0DDC) sets unk_60.unk_33C[2] |= 0x200000.
  - "NOUSE" (0x080E0DD4) sets unk_60.unk_33C[2] |= 0x100000.
- The NOSOUL bit is the gEwramData + 0x344 & 0x200000 test inside
  sub_08031F3C: with it set, only yellow souls of index at most 2
  (the basic stat records) spawn their effect entity — the "no soul"
  challenge flag.
- sub_08013404 (new-game init) saves and restores both flag bits
  around the unk_33C wipe, so the restriction is save-scoped.
- NOUSE's 0x100000 reader is not in the decompiled code (probably an
  unmatched soul-use routine). Patch 0844 wired the flags into the
  soul gates; the naming screen itself is ported.

## Patch 0836 - Held-soul sound deferred one frame (native ordering)

- The song table puts 0xBC, 0xBE and 0xBF on player 2, so same-frame
  replacement is native behaviour and 0xBE losing to 0xBC is correct.
- The held-soul sparkle's 0xBF is different: sub_08045164 requests it
  on the entity's first update, one frame after the collection's 0xBC.
  Emitting it in the same frame dropped 0xBC entirely. aria_runtime
  now defers it through deferred_sound, fired at the next
  update_entities pass — the same point in the frame order where the
  native entity update runs.

## Patch 0835 - Pause cursor entity mechanics decoded

- The pause-menu hand is a dedicated entity at gEwramData + 0xEB0,
  not a pool entity: sub_08048B0C fills it with the language's frame
  descriptor (0x08256EF8 or 0x0827B1F0), palette nibble 0xE through
  sub_0803B924 and an animation handle from sub_0803E654(2).
- sub_08048AD8 writes its position instantly every frame
  (column * 8 + 6, row * 8 + 3 in pixels) — there is no slide or
  tween when the selection changes, matching the runtime's direct
  placement.
- sub_08048018 adds the +-4px horizontal wiggle to the anchor's X:
  t = frame_counter >> 1, v = t & 7, offset = v - 3 while bit 3 of t
  is clear and 3 - v while set — algebraically identical to the
  runtime's ((cursor_tick >> 1) & 7) - 3 / 3 - (...) flip on
  (cursor_tick >> 4) & 1, verified term by term.
- The pointing-strip frames come from the descriptor's real animation:
  sub_0803F2C8 plays animation 0 of 0x08256EF8, a 29-step sequence of
  pose groups (records 2-8, 15-20, 9-14, 21-26 separated by record 2)
  with four-tick steps. draw_cursor now walks anim_frame/anim_duration
  instead of cycling seven records. The phase is driven by the shared
  cursor_tick rather than the entity's own anim player, so the sequence
  position is not reset on page open like the native entity's is.

## Patch 0834 - Death-state velocity bounce ported (sub_0801B03C)

- sub_0801B03C runs on Soma's own record during state 16 (the caller
  sets player +0x1E = 4): each axis' acceleration field is rewritten
  every frame to oppose its velocity sign at 0x200, then the
  velocity integrates it — a decay to a +-0x200 oscillation, so the
  corpse keeps drifting slowly instead of halting. The previous
  approach_zero model stopped both axes dead.
- death_state now writes friction/gravity_mod = +-0x200 by velocity
  sign and integrates directly (no sign-change clamp); vy decays at
  0x200/frame (~192 frames of drift) where the old model used
  gravity_mod 0x2000 (~12 frames).
- The +-0x200 terminal values are asserted in test_aos_soma; the
  every-four-frames sparkle emission stays in the runtime caller.

## Patch 0833 - Corpse sparkle uses the native animation 13

- sub_0801B03C's emitter calls sub_08045CEC(x, y, 0xD, 8): resource
  0x081C15F4, anim table 0x0820ED60, animation index 0xD (sequence
  13), callback sub_08045C9C (the drift bounce), entity slots
  0x49-0xCF. arg3's low nibble is OR'd into +0x5A bits 3-6 (the OBJ
  palette-row selector), while the colours come from the tileset's
  palette bank resolved by sub_08039614 — constant per
  (table, tileset) pair, so sequence 13 shares blood's bank 4.
- The death sparkle spawned AOS_EFFECT_SPARKLE (still frame 0x36,
  sub_08045B44 type 0) — wrong art. It now uses the new
  AOS_EFFECT_DEATH_SPARKLE kind: Effect/death_sparkle exports
  sequence 13 (identical frames to blood, same content hash), bank 4.
  Aria object export: 946 sequences, 2954 frames; golden re-recorded.
- Still approximate: the emitter entity's own +0x48/+0x4C bounce
  (sub_08045C9C's +-0x200 gravity flips) — our drift flag models the
  visible drift only.

## Patch 0832 - Death and game-over audio ported; reload branch decoded

- sub_0800C8C8 case 0 plays SONG_MUTE when the death sub-state

- GameModeGameOverUpdate's PlaySong calls are ported through a new

  sub_08011AD0, brightness decrease) and returns GAME_MODE_IN_GAME
  instead of GAME_OVER. The flag is never set in the decompiled

## Patch 0831 - Obtain/reward window decoded (not ported: no trigger)

- The post-combat obtain window is a game-mode state machine, not a

## Patch 0825 - Soul pickup trail spark (sub_08045B44 type 8)

- sub_080446D4's trail fully decoded at _08044756: after the collision

  sub_0802D5EC(0x200000) twice and adds each result to the soul's
  +0x40/+0x44 position (unsigned 0..32px offsets, no centering), then
  sub_08045B44(x, y, soul.+0x48>>6, soul.+0x4C>>6, 8,

  -soul velocity / 4 and acceleration +0x50/+0x54 = soul velocity / 64
  (both C-truncated divisions), and its +0x5C byte is copied from the
  soul.

  emit the spark on the same even-timer cadence with the same

## Patch 0818 - Cell framebuffer is VRAM; Item Use strips confirmed

- `sub_080412DC` stores the cell-drawing base at gEwramData+0x11598;
  its callers pass **VRAM addresses**, not EWRAM scratch: the pause
  menu uses 0x06004000 (sub_0805AE64, sub_08065484, sub_08067934),
  the Item Use page uses 0x06008000 (sub_08047520 region), Object1C
  uses 0x06005000. The literal 0x03001A18 seen inside the blitters is
  only the unset fallback. Glyph blits therefore write tile PIXEL DATA
  directly into a dedicated 32x32-tile VRAM sheet; there is no
  separate fb-to-VRAM copy pass.
- The tilemap side is static: pages pre-place strip entries with
  sub_08046DD4/46E04 that point into the text tile region, and
  sub_08046EF4/47098 write digit/dash tiles directly. Our
  cells_commit nibble-merge approximates this pipeline and produces
  the same visual result.
- sub_0804B6C4 strip coordinates fully decoded: description bars at
  tilemap (x=5, y=16..18) width 24 with tile ids 0x3200/0x3220/0x3240;
  slot strips at (x=2 and x=0x11, y=11..14) width 10 with ids
  0xCE00/0x3390 stepping 0x20 — matching our render_item_use layout.
- Context-A metrics confirmed in sub_08040E90: col unit 6 px
  (+0x115A6 = col*6), row unit 12 px (+0x115A8 = row*12).

## Patch 0805 - Lab learning loop v2: bandit, auto-states, real WRAM probes

- Framebuffer pixel format corrected to mGBA native 0xAABBGGRR
  (R in the low byte) across the shm mirror, PNG dump, PPM writer and
  the vision module — live videos and screenshots now show true colors.
- Worker loop reworked into a bandit: each trial picks an action by
  observed success rate (ties broken randomly) with epsilon
  exploration, for a total budget of `--iterations` trials across all
  actions instead of N per action sequentially.
- Inputs are now guaranteed: trials with no scripted keys get a random
  button/hold/at synthesized, so every trial is a real experiment.
- Novelty checkpoints: a never-seen scene hash auto-saves a new state
  blob (`auto_w<id>_<hash>`) parented to the trial's state.
- `--define-action` upserts by name; a built-in curriculum (walk
  left/right, jump, attack, random-input) engages when the actions
  table is empty.
- Verified WRAM map (EWRAM base 0x02000000, from cvaos decomp):
  gameMode=+0x10, inputData=+0x14, player entity = entityData[0] at
  +0x4E4 (pos whole X=+0x40 -> 0x02000524, Y=+0x44 -> 0x02000528),
  level=0x02013279, HP=0x0201327A, MP=0x0201327C, maxHP=0x0201327E,
  gold=0x02013290. Actions in lab.db now probe these addresses.
- `--scout` mode plays the game autonomously from boot: 600-frame
  chunks of A-taps/START for menus plus a RIGHT responsiveness pulse,
  storing every novel scene as a state blob and validating free
  gameplay only after two consecutive responsive chunks (real walking
  gives >4px per pulse; cutscene drift stays below). Early runs reach
  gameMode 4 and capture dozens of checkpoints; real free-roam
  validation is still being tuned.
- Exploration reward layer: every trial peeks 8 fixed WRAM regions
  (mode, area/room/song, position, HP/MP, XP/gold, level, item and
  soul inventories) before and after the run; compute_bonus scores
  new_scene, new_room (global fleet registry `lab.rooms`), new_area,
  new_area_song, item_found, soul_gained, level_up, exp_gain,
  gold_gain, clean_traverse, clean_move, ability_used, healed,
  damage, death. Bonuses feed `reward` and the bandit now selects
  actions by average reward, so exploration events steer learning.
  Waypoint restarts: ~25% of trials begin from a random stored
  checkpoint (scout finds, novel-scene auto states, manual records)
  so learning branches off the deepest states; the trial row records
  the actual starting state.
  Route reference: glitchless order — the agent must play normally,
  no movement exploits (Chapel -> Manticore/Ghost Dancers -> Study ->
  Great Armor -> Arena climb -> Balore/Forbidden Area -> Claimh ->
  Top Floor Graham -> Chaos). Souls are earned through normal combat
  and soul manipulation only where it is regular gameplay.
- Menu-aware scout: START is only sent while navigating title/menu
  phases; once mode 4 (free gameplay) is reached it is disabled, and
  a B tap closes any menu the previous chunk left open — fixes
  workers trapped in the START menu.
- OCR brick 2: `--glyphs DIR` one-shot mode runs 120 frames from a
  state and dumps every tile used by enabled text BGs as 8x8 PGM
  bitmaps plus per-BG ASCII tile-index maps (aos_vision_glyph_dump).
  Tile->char mapping still needs the font table (decomp too partial);
  next step is correlating dumps with known dialogue screens.
- OCR brick 1 live: every trial snapshots VRAM (96 KiB post-run
  peek) plus DISPCNT/BGCNT0..3 (session video_regs) and hashes each
  enabled text BG's 32x32 tile-index grid into metrics.tilemap,
  with txtrows (dense tile rows = text/UI lines) and tileuses.
  Glyph decoding still needs the font table; tile identity is now
  tracked per trial.
- Motion-based responsiveness: the session captures the framebuffer
  after frame 0 of every run (AosRunResult.fb_first); the scout now
  splits each chunk into a 520-frame text/menu phase and an 80-frame
  directional pulse, and validates free gameplay when >0.8% of
  central pixels change during the pulse (two consecutive chunks,
  mode 4). WRAM entity addresses proved unreliable for position —
  entityData[0] was empty in gameplay states. First validated
  checkpoint: scout_play_010.
- Per-trial motion metric (motion/mdir in metrics JSON) replaces the
  unreliable position probe; clean_move bonus now keys off screen
  motion. DB actions redefined without dead WRAM probes so the bandit
  learns purely from the reward layer (verified: clean_move bonuses
  flowing on scout_play_010 trials).
- Worker liveness: every trial/chunk updates worker.N.hb (epoch ms);
  the viewer flags any slot claiming to run with a heartbeat older
  than 15 s as STALE (red border). Workers self-detect stalls: 400
  consecutive zero-reward fails on the same scene, or 80 scout
  chunks without a novel scene, mark phase "stuck" and exit instead
  of spinning forever.
- DB purge: `aos_lab_worker --db X --purge` (also a Purge DB button
  in the viewer) deletes zero-reward fail trials, hopeless weight
  combos and auto checkpoints no trial ever referenced. The purge is
  aggressive and automatic: it caps unreferenced `scout_c*` scene
  states at the newest 100, deduplicates same-named `scout_c*` /
  `scout_play*` states (workers saving identical checkpoints),
  bounds `auto_*` states to the newest 50, and re-runs periodically
  inside long-running workers. States referenced by any trial are
  always kept.
- Game rules for the scout ("conscious AI"): the embedded policy now
  documents Aria controls in comments — D-pad moves, B jumps, A
  attacks/advances text, L/R are ability buttons, START opens the
  pause menu and must never be pressed during gameplay (mode 4), B
  closes menus, dialogue advances with A. Scout behavior follows it:
  START only before mode 4, B tap when gameplay exits to a menu,
  directional pulses for movement probing.
- Best-worker highlight: the viewer computes each worker's mean
  reward (worker.N.rsum / worker.N.rn meta, updated per trial) and
  draws a green outline on the top-performing slot.
- Smart restart on the best branch: every 60 trials (and on demand via
  the per-card "Best" button -> lab.control.N=best) a worker compares
  its reward EMA against the fleet's highest-value checkpoint
  (aos_labdb_best_state: state whose trials reached max reward) and
  hops to it when clearly behind; a 400-trial barren streak also hops
  branches (max 8 hops) before declaring stuck. Each worker persists
  its launch config in worker.N.launch so the viewer's Play buttons
  can respawn stopped workers: per-card Play/Best and fleet "Play
  all" (resume paused, respawn dead from stored config).
- Worker lifecycle in the viewer: each spawned child pid is tracked
  per slot; closing the window sends a cooperative stop and SIGTERM to
  every child unless the user enabled the background switch in
  Settings (lab.bg meta, off by default). With background on, workers
  keep running unsupervised and a later viewer reattaches through the
  shared database and framebuffer segments.
- The launch state picker lists only launch-worthy checkpoints
  (aos_labdb_valuable_states): the newest 40 scout_play_* checkpoints,
  manual records, and states whose trials scored reward > 0.5 —
  mirroring the purge keep-rules instead of dumping every scene state.
- Scout room awareness: each pulse chunk now also peeks the
  0x02000090 area/room block and marks every (area,room) reached in
  the shared lab.rooms registry (shown as rooms=N in the status), and
  every 6th chunk taps UP mid-pulse since Aria doors open with UP.
- Refined trial rules: ~15% of trials run 3x the frame budget so
  doors and room transitions are reachable, and a probe-fail that
  still earned exploration reward is recorded as "partial" instead of
  "fail" so the weight table does not treat it as a dead spin.
- Disk budget: scout scene dumps are capped at 80 per run, play
  checkpoints are saved only on scene change (or every 50 chunks),
  and trial auto-checkpoints at 120 per worker — novelty is still
  scored from the hash registry even when the blob is skipped.
- SQLite is kept effectively in RAM: synchronous=OFF,
  temp_store=MEMORY, wal_autocheckpoint=4000, mmap_size=1 GiB and a
  64 MiB page cache per connection.
- Purge now truly shrinks the registry: in addition to the dead-weight
  rules it keeps only the 300 highest-value states overall (best trial
  reward + scout_play/manual bonuses - scene-dump penalty), removes
  trials referencing deleted states and caps the trial log at the
  newest 8000 rows.
- Viewer hardening: store_row/log_append and every refresh_* bail out
  on NULL or invalid stores, turning the previous G_IS_LIST_STORE
  criticals + segfault path into no-ops.
- peeks + font tables from the decomp) but not implemented yet; the
  vision layer currently provides scene/HUD/text-presence signatures.

## Patch 0804 - Emulator lab supervision UI + per-trial visual signatures

- The GTK viewer now supervises up to eight live emulators: each worker
  mirrors its 240x160 framebuffer into a POSIX shared-memory segment
  (`/dev/shm/aoslab_fb_<id>`) and the viewer maps all eight into a 4x2
  grid of live `GtkPicture` videos at the top of the window.
- Window layout uses nested `GtkPaned` splitters (FileZilla-style):
  draggable divider between the video grid, the controls/log section
  and the registry tables.
- Every trial now records a visual signature in its `metrics` JSON via
  `aos_lab_vision`: whole-screen tile-grid hash, HUD strip hash,
  text-ink row count, distinct tile count, brightness and a 6x6x6 RGB
  histogram — persisted in the lab database alongside the probe
  metrics, giving each learning signal a scene fingerprint.
- Per-worker speed sliders (Auto..x16 = N*60 fps cap) are stored in
  `worker.<id>.speed` meta and applied per trial through
  `AosRunSpec.fps_cap`.
- `aos_lab_frame WORKER_ID OUT.png [SCALE]` dumps a worker's live
  shm framebuffer to PNG for external inspection (pure C + libpng).
- A global fleet bar adds Pause all / Resume all, Stop all and a
  global speed slider that writes every `worker.<id>.speed` at once;
  video cells keep the 3:2 aspect ratio (GTK_CONTENT_FIT_CONTAIN).

## Patch 0803 - Emulator laboratory: shared session, SQLite trials, GTK registry

- `aos_mgba_session` extracts the headless mGBA core (software renderer,
  frame stepping, key masks, PPM capture, save states, WRAM peeks) into a
  reusable C API shared by the lab tools.
- `aos_lab_db` is a local SQLite (WAL) store: state blobs, action
  definitions, trial outcomes and derived per-parameter success weights.
- `aos_lab_worker` is the automatic loop: it loads a state blob, applies
  an action with parameter jitter (hold/at ranges), scores the outcome
  through configurable memory probes, and records the trial plus its
  weight. An epsilon-greedy picker exploits the best-weighted parameter
  set or explores randomly (`--explore`).
- `aos_lab_viewer` (GTK4, ListView/ColumnView) polls the database and
  shows trials, weights, states and runs live, plus a Workers tab with
  eight parallel slots: each worker owns `worker.<id>.*` meta keys and
  a `lab.control.<id>` pause/resume/stop channel, and the viewer can
  spawn batches (`--worker-id`, iterations, latest state) directly.
  The lab database lives in `database/` (gitignored), a symlink to the
  bulk-storage directory so states, trials and worker logs stay off the
  system drive; the viewer defaults to `database/lab.db`. The viewer
  shows eight colour-coded worker cards with pause/resume/stop, a batch
  launcher (worker slot, save-state picker, trial count), a save-state
  recorder, a per-worker speed slider (Auto = unthrottled, 1-16 caps
  emulation at that multiple of 60 fps via `AosRunSpec.fps_cap`), and a
  live log streamed in memory — worker stdout is piped into the window
  and never written to disk.
- Verified locally: state capture from boot, action definition, trial
  batches, weight accumulation and two parallel workers with isolated
  control channels all work end to end. Gameplay probes still need real
  WRAM addresses; menu scripts for the intro are open.

## Patch 0802 - Headless mGBA reference runner (aos_mgba_lab)

- New C tool `src/tools/aos_mgba_lab.c` (target `aos_mgba_lab`) drives
  the pinned Aria ROM through the system libmgba core API: frame stepping,
  scripted key masks, PPM screenshots, mGBA save states in/out and typed
  WRAM peeks. It is the first piece of the emulator laboratory used to
  compare the recreation against the real game frame by frame.
- Verified locally: the tool boots the ROM headless (no BIOS image),
  produces real 240x160 frames, navigates title -> file flow -> in-game
  room with scripted START/A presses, and save-state round-trips work.
- Still open: save-state trial database with success/reward tracking,
  input-replay learning loop, GTK viewer, and menu-navigation
  calibration for reaching the scrolling introduction reliably.
- mGBA sources are not vendored yet; the tool links the system
  `libmgba-dev` package. ROM/save-state/screenshot outputs stay local
  and untracked.

## Patch 0801 - Export and draw Aria SPECIAL objects with verified ids

- Dumped the ROM create table `sUnk_084F0DF8`: the kind-2 entity id is
  the table index, and the decompiler's `ObjectNN` suffix is the hex id
  (`Object13Create` = id 0x13 = 19). The first export pass had attached
  each sheet to a decimal-shifted id; the specs were remapped to the
  true ids 13, 16, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 25 and 27 after matching every
  create address to its label and `sub_0806E0D0` arguments.
- `sub_0806E0D0(entity, gfx, palette, bank, frames)` is decoded: ids
  with hard-coded resources export directly; ids 14 and 18 index
  param0-driven resource tables (`0x085262BC` records -> `0x08526214`
  triples, and `0x085263A8` 8-byte records), id 15 uses the shared flame
  frames `0x0820ED60` with a param0-selected palette row, id 17 is a
  spawner (`EntityCreateInRange` + self-delete) and ids 7/10 dispatch
  indirectly — all decoded but not yet exported.
- The nine verified specs export as `Object/special_NN/anim_M`
  sequences with `metadata/object_frames.tsv`
  (`metroidvania-aos-object-frames-v1`); empty native animations are
  skipped (846 sequences / 2425 frames). The runtime loads them into
  `special_objects[64]` and draws each spawned SPECIAL entity with
  animation 0 looping; per-object animation/behaviour selection is not
  yet audited.
- Param0 census across all rooms (`--aria-entities`): id 14 uses record
  indices 0-14, id 18 uses 0-3, id 15 is mostly param0 0 plus palette
  variants 0x600/0x900, id 7 is mostly param0 1. The ROM tables are
  decoded: id 14's `entity+0x30` indexes 12-byte records at
  `0x085262BC` whose byte0 selects a `{gfx,palette,frames}` triple at
  `0x08526214 + group*12` (groups 0-13) and byte1 the palette bank;
  id 18's param0 indexes 24-byte records at `0x085263A8`
  (gfx@0, palette@4, frames@8, bank@0xC); id 15 draws the shared flame
  frames `0x0820ED60` with palette row `param0 >> 8` (default 7).
- Param0-driven variants are now exported and drawn: id 14's fifteen
  room-used records (0-14) resolve through `0x085262BC`/`0x08526214` to
  fourteen sprite groups plus a palette-bank twin, and id 18's four
  records at `0x085263A8` export as `Object/special_14_vNN` and
  `Object/special_18_vNN`. The runtime keeps `special_variants[24]`,
  matches `entity->param0` to the `_vP` suffix and falls back to the
  base `special_objects` art. The export grew to 874 sequences / 2484
  frames; the golden fixture was regenerated. Id 15's shared-flame path
  (`0x0820ED60` + palette row `param0 >> 8`) and the indirect creates
  of ids 7 and 10 remain open.
- Id 15's shared-flame path is now exported: `sub_0803AFB8` resolves the
  tile sheet `0x081C15F4`'s palette slot to the 16-bank palette
  `0x0826F8A4` (the state-3 alternative `0x082718A8` is not selected for
  Soma — divergence noted) and `sub_0803B924` draws the shared frames
  `0x0820ED60` with OBJ palette row `param0 >> 8` (default 7). Three
  variants export as `special_15_v6/v7/v9`; the runtime compares
  `(param0 >> 8) ?: 7` for this id and animation 0 is the shared flame
  look. The export grew to 940 sequences / 2931 frames. The indirect
  creates of ids 7 and 10 remain open.
- Ids 7 and 10 are logic objects, not sprites: `Object07Create` (id 7)
  dispatches `param0` through a 5-case jump table (the dominant
  `param0=1` only clears `+0x10`; cases 0/2 spawn children via
  `sub_0804F374` indexed by `param1` through `0x085255AC`), and
  `Object0ACreate` (id 10) is an entity spawner dispatching
  `param0 & 0xFF` through 36-byte records at `0x080E9644`, deleting
  itself when the `+0x37E` bit is clear. Neither calls
  `sub_0806E0D0`, so there is no object art to export; their behaviour
  ports remain open. Sprite coverage of the SPECIAL layer is complete.
- Regenerated the `aos_native_golden` fixture for the corrected object
  outputs. Source-derived and unit-tested, not emulator-compared.

Next: audit each object's animation/state selection (id 15's brain
`sub_08050F08`, the `sub_0803F2C8` animation argument, the id 7/10
behaviours) and compare a room's object layer against an emulator.

## Patch 0782 - Held title pulses climb one semitone per beat

- While X or Y stays held on the shared title screen, each 0.5-second
  pulse now starts six semitones below the native pitch and rises one
  semitone per beat, saturating at +12; releasing the key resets the
  progression for the next hold. The 0.5-second timing and the visual
  pulse are unchanged.
- Aria: `aos_mp2k_player_pitch()` writes the host-only
  `key_shift_public` control on the pulse player's active tracks
  (player 3 for `0x081`). Pitch-sensitive channels retune through
  `key_shift_calculated`, and the fixed-frequency (type 8) channels —
  the only kind song `0x081` uses — are retimed by a host-only 16.16
  playback step derived from the same control, leaving native pitch
  state untouched.
- Zero Mission: `mzm_audio_set_player_pitch()` stores a per-player
  semitone offset applied inside the native pitch routine
  (`unk_4eb4`), so both DirectSound and PSG voices retune; it covers
  the `0x1DC` player without affecting music player 0.
- Tests: the split test covers the -6/+12 progression and the
  press/release reset, the MP2K test covers per-player track
  transposition and the fixed-frequency retiming, and the MZM engine
  test measures a higher PSG sign-change rate at +12 semitones.

  5 and every browser entry). `init`, `set_bank` and `load_bank` now share one
  `engine_replace` routine that restores the 0xFF defaults; failed loads still
  report their error and leave the previous engine untouched.

  `set_bank` and `load_bank`, per-player muting in the mixer, failed-load
  preservation, and a real-bank check that song `0x11C` (player 5) renders
  nonzero PCM. All 72 silent table entries were audited: every one is a
  legitimate zero-track ROM entry, so no CGB/PSG path is implicated.
- `fusion_sfx_browser` now reports bank, table, device and player-start
  failures on stderr/status, and `--check` renders both title pulses offline

- Source-derived and unit-tested, not emulator-compared. The native damage
  number entity (`sub_08042B8C`), CGB synthesis, reverb and audio LFOs remain
  open.

## Patch 0750 - Port Object20's collision-guided Skeleton Knight flight

- Completed `sub_0805E5D4`'s state-2 path for type-10 children with parameter
  bit 3. Its animation-1 setup and `0xA0` opportunity counter now precede
  the native one-in-two movement gate.
- Reproduced the relevant `sub_0806E140` behavior: each accepted update
  tentatively moves a quarter pixel toward the facing side and two pixels
  down. Open air restores X and keeps the fall; floor contact retains its
  horizontal fraction plus any wall correction and snaps Y by the collision
  depth. Odd RNG results leave both motion and the counter unchanged.
- Added injected floor-depth and wall-push queries beside RNG, sine and
  ArcTan2. The Aria host connects them to the active room's portable collision
  layer, while tests and future editor previews can supply deterministic
  geometry without depending on SDL or a loaded room. No current Object20
  emission record sets bit 3, so
  this completes the generic private-child path without changing the visible
  opening sequence. Source-derived tests cover air, floor, both facings and
  the skipped RNG clock; emulator comparison remains outstanding and the
  scene stays partial.

## Patch 0748 - Port Object20's emitted attack tails

- Replaced the fixed 48-frame retirement of Object20's emitted actors with

## Patch 0747 - Drive Object20's emitted native motion

- Added host-injected RNG and sine callbacks to the portable opening-scene
  controller. The game runtime supplies the existing native-formula
  `aos_random` and `aos_sine` primitives, while tests and future editor
  previews can provide deterministic callbacks without acquiring an SDL or
  gameplay-runtime dependency.
- Ported the source-visible states 0-2 of `sub_0805E2D8` for Object20's type-8
  Winged Skeletons. Creation takes `(RNG & 0x7F) << 9` as the phase, then each
  frame samples `sin(phase + 0x4000) / 4` with the native negative rounding,
  advances the phase by `0x200` and follows the parent-bit-8 handoff through
  states 0, 1 and 2.
- Ported the non-collision states 0-2 of `sub_0805E5D4` for its type-10
  Skeleton Knights. Every entity waits on its recorded `0..6` selector; those
  without parameter bit 1 wait a second time, then consume sixteen successful
  one-in-three clocks while rising by half a pixel. Parameter bits 3 and 4
  select animations 1 and 2 on entry to state 2.
- Deterministic tests cover RNG consumption, phase and fixed-point Y changes,
  stagger states, timers and a variant that must remain waiting. A reviewed
  offscreen frame confirms the actors remain composed in the panned room after
  this motion pass. The parameter-bit-3 collision flight, post-blink random
  collision checks, attacks and particle tails remain absent, so the feature
  stays partial and not emulator-compared.

## Patch 0744 - Drive Object20's timed actor and audio beats

- Corrected the dialogue protocol for control `02`: `sub_08067A04` advances
  Object20's callback state and continues parsing, while the following control
  `05` owns the input wait. The earlier controller incorrectly inserted a
  second confirmation at every one of the seven scene beats. Printable text
  now also exits after one visible glyph per frame instead of collapsing the
  rest of a page into a single frame while A is pressed.
- `AosOpeningActors` now accepts those semantic beats independently of SDL,
  resets each actor's animation clock and consumes animation durations supplied
  by the exported object library. Runtime and future editor previews therefore
  share the same deterministic scene controller without embedding extracted
  frames or timing manifests in source.
- The source-visible `sub_0805D410` timing is connected: the reveal waits
  `0x20` frames before Mina animation 5 and sound `0x1B4`; Arikado uses
  animations 2 and 3 with sound `0x1DF`, the first animation's real duration,
  a `0x10`-frame pause and sound `0x1E0`; the battle waits `0x10`, starts its
  `0xD2` timer, hides the Winged Skeleton with `0x6B` at `0xD0`, then requests
  the soul-impact sound `0x197` at `0x8F`.
- Rendering now uses per-actor animation ages rather than one global modulo,
  so every beat visibly restarts its selected animation. Deterministic tests
  cover each boundary and the corrected no-extra-confirmation script flow; a
  private verified-ROM pass still reaches all seven beats. The missing room
  reveal transition, spawned visual effects, attack entity and soul particle
  keep the feature partial and source-derived rather than emulator-validated.

## Patch 0733 - Launcher fixes and Aria's audio delay

- Spamming START at the start no longer freezes the shared title: the press
  sent to Zero Mission's title now waits for a released key, Zero Mission
  counts as ready only once its title reads START (unk_f, after 30 idle
  frames), and a chosen title that does not leave gives the line back after
  3 s.

  select (and any return to a game's own title) comes back to the shared
  title in the same window, as many times as wanted (checked with scripted
  round trips). New `--frontend-arg` for such scripted runs.
- Aria's sound streams (menu preview, gameplay runtime, launcher) are fed
  one 176-sample frame a host frame, so they are now declared at 60 x 176 =
  10560 Hz (AOS_MP2K_HOST_RATE) instead of 10512 Hz, whose queue grew by
  48 samples a second (a delay of a quarter second after a minute), and
  their queue is capped at four frames.

## Patch 0702 - Elements, statuses and petrification

- `sub_08021654` now takes the hit's elements:
  - a resisted element quarters the damage instead of halving it;
  - the stone status doubles it;
  - 0x13260 bit 0x2000 evades the hit (0x13B);
  - 0xB3 is played for each hurt;
  - the element bits 6-8 set poison, curse or stone, with the 0x080E1338
    timers (600, 600, 15 presses) and sounds 0x198 then 0xAE, 0xAD or
    0xB1, unless all the matching resistances are held.
- The status part of `sub_08021994` runs every frame:
  - stone presses wear the stone off (0xB0, 0xAF);
  - the poison and curse timers run out;
  - poison quarters STR, CON and INT;
  - curse drains max MP / 128 every 4 frames instead of regenerating.
- A petrified Soma enters state 15 (`sub_08019BB0`, animations 0x49 /
  0x4A).
- The grenade (2), a gold Medusa Head and the Gorgon breath (0x100) now
  carry their contact elements.
- Gargoyle's resistance 0x100 quarters those hits and refuses their
  stone; Zombie's soul works on a poisoned Soma. Both monsters are now
  complete (37), although no ported enemy poisons yet. Zero Mission is
  unchanged.

## Patch 0680 - Buer side-gated linked-fire mirror during attacks

## Patch 0602 - Aria MP2K track event decoder

- New host-neutral `aos_mp2k` code advances one sequencer clock at a time.
  It reproduces the 49-entry wait and note clock table, running status, note
  parameters, EOT, FINE, absolute GOTO, three nested PATT/PEND calls and
  counted or infinite REPT branches.
- The source-derived PRIO, TEMPO, KEYSH, VOICE, VOL, PAN, BEND, BENDR, LFOS,
  LFODL, MOD, MODT and TUNE commands update deterministic track state.
  Bounds checks reject bad stream pointers, excessive command loops and the
  still-unported PORT and XCMD events. Synthetic tests cover waits, notes,
  retained running parameters, patterns, repeats and failure paths.
- This decoder is intentionally not connected to `StartSong` yet: the
  private MP2K bank, song-header track initialization, tempo scheduler,
  voice allocation, sample mixer and SDL sink remain absent. Audio and Axe
  Armor's sound aspect stay `partial`; nothing is audible yet. Source-derived
  and unit-tested, not emulator-compared. Zero Mission is unchanged.

## Patch 0601 - Aria native song-table export and runtime routing

- `src/assets/aos/sound.c` reads all 495 entries of Aria's `gSongTable` and
  the fixed fields of every MP2K header. The new `aria_sound` rebuild task
  writes a private manifest with the header pointer, player, channel, track
  count, block count, priority and reverb; its complete output is guarded by
  the native golden digest without committing ROM-derived data.
- `aos_audio_load_song_table` validates and installs the real player and
  priority routing metadata. The room runtime loads it before `PlaySong` and
  calls `MPlayVolumeUpdate` once per lifecycle frame. Synthetic tests cover
  failed and successful loading, while the local-ROM asset test checks
  known entries on players 0, 1, 2 and 6.
- Playback is still inaudible: the MP2K track interpreter, voice and sample
  banks, mixer and SDL sink are not ported. Axe Armor's sound aspect remains
  `partial`, no monster becomes complete, and the audio feature remains
  `partial`. Source-derived and unit-tested, not emulator-compared. Zero
  Mission is unchanged.

  Mission is unchanged.

## Patch 0599 - Aria PlaySong requests and Axe Armor sound events

- `src/runtime/aos/core/aos_audio.c` introduces a host-neutral, tested boundary for
  Aria's `PlaySong`: table IDs below 0x400 become start requests,
  `STOP_SONG` masks the ID, and other values become audio-command requests.
  Requests are logged and may be forwarded to a sink.
- Axe Armor now requests 0x86 when its thrown axe is struck, 0x6F when its
  death begins and 0x6E at each eighth-frame spark. `SkillAxeArmorUse`
  requests 0xE3 when the red-soul axe is created. Their exact event counts
  and ordering have ROM-free regression tests.
- This is request routing, not audible playback: Aria's song table, M4A
  sequencer, native samples, mixer and SDL output remain absent. Axe Armor's
  sound aspect therefore moves from `missing` to `partial`; no monster is
  complete yet. Source-derived and unit-tested, not emulator-compared. Zero
  Mission is unchanged.

## Patch 0574 - Render Aria's native main-menu backgrounds

- Added a shared bounded ROM graphics loader for raw and compressed native
  graphics descriptors and palettes, and moved the introduction renderer onto
  it without changing its output.
- Connected the main menu's complete palette, two shared character banks and
  the English, French or German character bank. The frontend now renders the
  three native background planes for the base selector and the PLAY, COPY,
  DELETE and name-entry screens, including BG2's 10:6 alpha composition.
- Fixed lifecycle language propagation so a confirmed Reset selection chooses
  the corresponding main-menu bank instead of treating the save-request flag
  as a language identifier.
- Synthetic tests cover decompression, VRAM placement, palette conversion and
  all 15 screen planes. The optional hash-gated ROM smoke test validates all
  three languages without exporting pixels, and a local SDL review reached
  the live MAIN_MENU controller and confirmed the native background render.
- File names, slot statistics, cursors and prompts still use the host's dynamic
  text overlay because the menu entity/OAM text streams are not ported. Native
  title artwork is also still absent, so the feature remains partial.
  Source-derived and unit-tested, not emulator-compared. Zero Mission and
  audio are unchanged.
- Next: render the main menu's dynamic entity/OAM and text streams so the host
  overlay can be removed, then connect the native title graphics.

## Patch 0573 - Render Aria's native introduction backgrounds

- Added a bounded in-memory loader for the introduction's complete 16-row
  background palette, its two compressed 8 KiB character banks and the three
  native block-map metadata records. The loader reuses the C11 Aria tilemap
  decoder and renderer and never exports ROM-derived pixels.
- The SDL frontend now draws BG3, BG2 and BG1 in native priority order over
  palette color zero, wraps their 256-pixel-wide planes and follows the three
  fixed-point vertical positions from `GameModeIntroCutsceneUpdate`. The text
  plane now uses color 8 from native palette row 15 instead of a fixed host
  color.
- Synthetic tests cover compressed resource headers, VRAM placement, block-map
  expansion, palette conversion and all three layers. The optional hash-gated
  ROM smoke check validates the native 256x512, 256x768 and 256x512 planes
  without unresolved tiles; a local SDL review confirmed the scrolling scene
  and text together.
- The six introduction actors still lack their sprite graphics, OAM animation
  and affine rendering. Alpha interaction with those actors and emulator pixel
  comparison are therefore open, so the feature remains partial.

## Patch 0572 - Render Aria's native introduction font

  draws their 12 bitmap rows into a 32-by-32 GBA 4bpp tile canvas and preserves
  both horizontal tile splitting and vertical tile-row transitions.

  not emulator-compared. Zero Mission and audio are unchanged.

## Patch 0518 - Native Zero Mission export tables and background image

- Ported the export's `background.bmp` renderer exactly
  (`fusion_mzm_render_export_background`): the older diagnostic path of
  `scripts/mzm_room_render.py` that `produce()` uses, not the VRAM
  selection. It draws only the tileset's own metatiles (common blocks such
  as hatches stay black, since the runtime animates them from the
  `H/V/A` records), takes tiles from the decompressed tileset graphics at
  the character base inferred from BG1 (`graphic_base`: 192, or 704 with
  more coverage), maps BG rows 3 to 15 to source palette rows 1 to 13, paints
  color 0 without making it visible, and composes BG1 over BG2 only when
  BG2's property is exactly `BG_PROP_RLE_COMPRESSED` (`BG_PROP_MOVING`
  layers are not composed). A room whose BG1 reaches no tile graphics is
  reported as skipped, like the Python `ValueError`. The new
  `--mzm-export-backgrounds` command and a real-ROM equivalence test match
  all 330 exportable rooms' bitmaps byte for byte (265,300,380 bytes), with
  synthetic coverage of composition, the `BG_PROP_MOVING` rule, painted
  color 0, common blocks and the skip.

- Added `fusion_mzm_serialize_block_tables` for `blocks.tsv`: the action
  damage types, block behaviors (with the `isSpeedboost` / `isBombChain` bit
  fields), weaknesses, reforming tiles, broken-block timers, tank behaviors
  and the start/total/increase tank lists, the bomb-chain tables and every
  raw Clipdata value's collision and behavior, read from the bounded
  `block_data.c` ELF objects. Element counts come from the object sizes;
  the `makesolid` / `tankclip` Clipdata values and `DIFF_NORMAL` are named
  constants of the decompilation, and `MESSAGE_NONE` (0xFF) prints as -1
  like its enum value.
- Added `fusion_mzm_serialize_power_bomb_windows` for `power_bomb.tsv`: the
  s16 window values of every `sHaze_PowerBomb_WindowValuesPointers` entry.
- The new `--mzm-runtime-tables` command and a real-ROM equivalence test
  match `block_table_lines` (4,643 bytes) and `power_bomb_window_lines`
  (201,326 bytes) byte for byte, with synthetic coverage of the bit fields,
  the signed message and offsets, the difficulty rows and malformed sizes.
- Every private file of the Zero Mission room export except the export
  index now has a byte-identical native serializer: `room.tsv`,
  `background.bmp`, `bg0.bmp` / `bg3.bmp`, the tileset sheets, `blocks.tsv`
  and `power_bomb.tsv`. Production authority and gameplay status do not
  change; the native writer, the export index and the rebuild cutover come
  next.

- Next: use the verified game identity to select one small game-specific native
  metadata table and compare it against a Python fixture.

## Patch 0482 - C11 GBA header metadata reader

- Added a bounded native reader for the standard GBA title, game code, maker
  code, unit/device and software-version fields.
- Added complement-checksum calculation and a fixed-header-marker check while
  preserving the raw metadata bytes in caller-owned, NUL-terminated fields.
- Added a ROM-free synthetic-header CTest and a Python fixture that compares
  the native `fusion_importer --header` output field by field.
- This is an input-contract foundation only; Python remains authoritative for
  extraction and no gameplay or resource-equivalence status changed.
- Next: connect verified ROM identity to this metadata reader, then port one
  small game-specific metadata table before touching room extraction.

## Patch 0481 - C11 GBA binary and compression primitives

- Added a reusable bounds-checked little-endian binary reader to
  `fusion_assets`.
- Added strict-output GBA BIOS 0x10 LZ77 and 0x30 RLE decoders with malformed
  stream, backreference, truncation and destination-bound checks.
- Added ROM-free CTest coverage for literals, overlapping LZ77 copies, RLE,
  endianness and invalid input.
- These primitives are not connected to a production extractor yet; Python
  remains authoritative and no resource-equivalence claim is made.
- Next: port one small metadata reader using the binary reader and compare its
  output structurally against the existing Python extractor.

## Patch 0480 - C11 asset pipeline foundation

- Added the `fusion_assets` C11 library with bounded ROM loading, exact 8 MiB
  size checks, SHA-1 verification for the pinned USA Zero Mission and Aria
  revisions, clear errors and zeroing on release.
- Added `fusion_importer`: `--list`, `--verify`, and an explicit `--dry-run`
  task-plan interface. `--assets` and `--all` report the current boundary
  instead of pretending that extraction has already migrated.
- Added the first migration matrix in `docs/ASSET_PIPELINE_MIGRATION.md` and
  documented the public contract in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Python extractors, generated caches and ROM-derived resources remain
  unchanged and authoritative; no gameplay parity status was raised.
- Next: add generic bounded GBA binary/decompression primitives, then port one
  small metadata extractor with a Python/C equivalence fixture.

## Patch 0479 - Aria save-room checkpoints

- Added `aos_save_room`, a device-free controller for the native Object1C
  activation rectangle (`x=104..136`, `y=128..183`) and its Up edge.
- Runtime room exports now use schema version 4 with global-map save and warp
  flags. Existing version-3 private exports remain readable and their Object1C
  records still identify save rooms.
- In a detected save room, Up restores Soma's HP and atomically writes the
  selected portable file's room, spawn, HP, movement mask and play time. A
  small procedural marker makes the host checkpoint visible without importing
  ROM-derived graphics.
- Native healing animation, save Yes/No prompt, object art, audio, inventory,
  event/map flags and the original SRAM format remain intentionally partial.
- Next: port the first pause/status inventory state and then extend the save
  record only as its native owners become available.

## Patch 0478 - Aria file selection and runtime launch bridge

- Replaced the New Game and Continue placeholders in the SDL title host with
  three selectable files, empty/occupied summaries and overwrite confirmation.
- Added a checksummed, versioned and ROM-free host save format. New Game
  creates area 0, room 0 state, while Continue loads the selected file's room,
  spawn, HP and currently exposed movement abilities into `fusion_aria_runtime`.
- The title host launches the actual sibling runtime process after selection;
  `--runtime` and `--save-dir` keep this testable with explicit local paths.
- This is a playable host bridge, not a claim that native Aria SRAM or
  `GameModeMainMenuUpdate` is complete. Inventory, equipment, souls, flags,
  play-time updates and writes from native save rooms remain unported.
- Next: connect native save-room detection and interaction to this save model,
  then add the first pause/status inventory state without touching audio.

## Current product state

The repository is a native-content reconstruction and editor project. It is not
yet a playable crossover and contains no active simulated or emulator-backed
game frontend.

| Area | State | Verified boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Story | Data baseline | Complete campaign bible and dependency-checked parallel timeline |
| Boss inventory | Verified native identities | 9 MZM encounters and all 11 Aria campaign bosses source/ROM-mapped |
| Savepoints | Verified metadata | 29 MZM platform rooms and 17 Aria map-flag rooms |
| MZM rooms | Partial, systematically audited | 331 descriptors: 330 partial renders, 1 unsupported sentinel, 0 errors |
| Aria rooms | Partial, systematically audited | 343 descriptors: 342 partial renders, 1 unsupported affine/non-text room, 0 errors |
| Character assets | Partial | canonical local Samus runtime library: 1,072 indexed sequences, 2,640 unique BMPs; 566 projectile sequences; Soma preview extraction |
| GTK4 editor | Active | shared room documents, native-data overlays, catalog and area/world render audits |
| Headless backend | Active foundation | stable CLI envelope plus room, tile, collision, door, transition, entity, story and audit operations |
| Native gameplay engines | Experimental MZM and Aria runtimes | MZM now boots through the intro, title and file select into its room runtime, with a broad but incomplete set of Samus systems, enemies and the Deorem, Acid Worm, Gadora, Imago Larva, Kraid, Ridley and Mother Brain encounters. Aria remains an experimental room/combat runtime. Neither campaign is complete and the crossover host is not implemented. |
| Dual-character AI | Not started | story/design requirement only |
| Cross-world travel | Not started | savepoint metadata exists; no native runtime loader |

## Verified commands

Run after each change:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build -j2
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
python3 scripts/check_no_proprietary.py
```

The latest exact result is recorded in the corresponding commit handoff.

Cleanup validation on 2026-10-08: the reduced CMake project built without
warnings, CTest passed `5/5`, the consolidated Python suite passed `82/82`, the
GTK4 editor survived a three-second Xvfb smoke run, and the proprietary-file
guard passed. The active editor binary has no mGBA linkage.

Patch 0048 validation on 2026-10-08: CTest passed `5/5`, the Python suite passed
`85/85`, the exact-ROM Aria import completed with 343 rooms and 2,336 entities,
and the proprietary-file guard passed.

## Immediate priorities

1. Migrate active historical asset paths one consumer group at a time.
2. Replace the Samus compatibility discovery adapter with one generic native scanner.
3. Map suits, transitions and action priorities from verified native data.
4. Build an equivalent automated Soma/Aria extraction pipeline.
5. Define both native engine adapter contracts around validated exported data.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- Never track ROMs, saves or extracted proprietary assets.
- Never mutate ROMs or upstream submodules.
- Never substitute fake geometry for missing original data without an explicit
  diagnostic label.
- Never call extracted metadata a completed native gameplay feature.

  are required before it can be enabled for either world.

## Unified player systems - accepted requirements, pending implementation

- One character-independent capability interface: acquired powers, abilities,
  inventory flags, unlock conditions and per-world game mechanics.
- Player-specific presentation and rules: Samus upgrades, ammo/energy and
  equipment versus Soma souls, MP/HP, attributes, items and abilities.
- One status/menu framework with different views, stats and controls depending
  on which playable character is active. No fabricated equivalence of stats.
- Native controller support, configurable mapping, keyboard/controller parity,
  in-editor input preview and runtime gamepad navigation; SDL3 input backend
  must be attached only once engine input/action contracts exist.
- Cross-world abilities, room requirements and cutscene/event conditions must
  reference a shared canonical schema with world-specific adapters and checks.
- Export only project-authored assets. Never write ROMs or claim unfinished
  player systems exist in native gameplay yet.

## Patch 0057 - GTK4 room browser context lifetime

- Fixed a GTK4 ownership violation in the shared Zero/Aria browser: the
  future Create room popover was parented directly to GtkListBox. GTK4 expects
  GtkListBoxRow children, and filtering may dereference non-row widgets.
- A GtkOverlay now owns the popover, while the scrolled room list remains the
  overlay's regular child. Right-click popup coordinates are translated from
  the list into the overlay's coordinate space.
- The browser GTK regression now checks popover parenting for both games and
  repeats browser creation/destruction. Local GTK4 build and CTest must confirm.

  instead of placing a `GtkPopover` in a `GtkOverlay` allocation slot.
- The right-click shortcut opens the same anchored menu. Authored-room creation
  remains disabled until its native engine adapter and schema exist.
- The GTK test now emits progress diagnostics around both browsers' creation
  and removal, to identify the failing phase if a crash persists.
- A successful GTK4 build/CTest run on Debian is required before committing.

## Patch 0061 - GTK4 browser teardown ownership

- The shared Aria/Zero browser explicitly retains the filtered list and its

  not a change to private room data or playable world geometry.

- The supplied GDB trace stopped during GTK settings initialization, not the
  CTest Aria tab-removal crash; run the debugger with CTest's isolated

## Patch 0062 - GTK4 dropdown model ownership

- The page teardown crash was reproduced in GDB at
  `g_list_model_get_n_items()`, via the browser's dropdown release.
- The GTK regression now checks both area models (8 and 13 entries)
  and changes their selections before removing the two tabs.
- Build, all six CTest cases, and the proprietary-file guard require
  validation on the developer's Debian GTK4 environment.

## Patch 0063 - shared private authored-room draft contract

- Added a strict versioned `metroidvania.authored-room` schema shared by Zero
  Mission and Aria, with stable world/area/slug identity and explicit metadata
  separating project-authored geometry from verified original ROM content.
- New `scripts.authored_rooms` can create, validate and list draft documents
  under ignored `assets/extracted/authored_rooms/<world>/<area>/`. Files are
  create-only, with duplicate rejection, input bounds and symlink guards.

  `draft_not_playable`; game export fails closed until native engine adapters
  and spatial/collision validation exist.

  duplicate IDs, malformed drafts and engine-readiness misrepresentation.
- **The GTK Create room action is intentionally still disabled**. The next
  step is connecting the common authoring form and editable project-owned
  room layers to this contract, then validated native engine adapters.
- Developer GTK4, CTest and proprietary-file verification remain required.

## Patch 0109 - deferred GTK room changes

## Patch 0112 - chronological shared room undo

- One per-tab chronological Undo/Redo history captures a source-independent

  removes the temporary draft, and redo restores it without ROM changes.
- A snapshot matching the last saved/opened state removes the dirty star.

- GTK/Xvfb regression exercises Tile -> JSON -> Undo twice -> Redo twice.
  Native source encoders and atomic multi-file disk commits remain pending.

## Patch 0113 — fixed room toolbar and collision authoring
